bug_semantics: The advisory defines one vulnerability with an antecedent insecure initialization and an additional consent-flow coupling: OpenAM ships the iPlanetDirectoryPro bearer-session cookie with com.sun.identity.cookie.httponly=false and no SameSite default, so same-origin script can read and replay it and cross-site exposure is wider; OAuth/OIDC consent additionally used that same SSO token value as its csrf form value. The 16.1.1 patch breaks the consent-token reuse and adds SameSite=Lax and protocol-derived Secure, but the shipped HttpOnly=false default remains in 16.1.1.
flaw_origin: The smallest real commit that originally wrote the headline com.sun.identity.cookie.httponly=false default cannot be reconstructed in this clone. The earliest object containing it is parentless SVN tag snapshot 0dbc9205d83b7d14e5eadd12606e568df249258e, and later occurrences are snapshots, imports, or moves rather than eligible BICs. Commit 4f04731207681973251c52436f07118e7c325e88 is a valid atomic BIC only for the secondary 2016 OAuth/OIDC coupling: it creates CsrfProtection.java, reads the SSO cookie in OAuth2ConsentPageHelper.js, and submits that value from main-authorize.js. It cannot replace the absent BIC for the earlier insecure cookie initialization that the advisory names first and classifies as CWE-1004/CWE-1188.
ai_marker: unavailable: there is no eligible commit object for the true BIC that first wrote com.sun.identity.cookie.httponly=false. The parentless SVN tag snapshot, later imports/moves, secondary OAuth BIC 4f04731207681973251c52436f07118e7c325e88, and fix object are not substitutes under the BIC-only attribution rule.
evidence: The bundle's first-party GHSA describes an Insecure Default Initialization that ships iPlanetDirectoryPro with HttpOnly=false, then separately says the cookie is also reused as the OAuth/OIDC CSRF token; it declares versions through 16.0.6 affected and 16.1.1 patched. Re-run `git grep -n -F 'com.sun.identity.cookie.httponly=false' 0dbc9205d83b7d14e5eadd12606e568df249258e` found the default at opensso/products/amserver/war/xml/template/sms/serverdefaults.properties:47. `git cat-file commit 0dbc9205d83b7d14e5eadd12606e568df249258e` showed no parent and message `Tag for 9.5.1 RC2` with git-svn-id revision 389, so it is a boundary snapshot, not the writing commit. `git log --all --reverse --format='%H %P %s' -S'com.sun.identity.cookie.httponly=false' --` began with multiple parentless tag snapshots; later 94cdb6ea929e1d7232a268aacb435b86cb78a787 has parent 837871e12425577ebe5d6f129d18ea78dd0e640e and message `moved tempolate into webapp`, while 5c099afa7c9361afc2f4477fec0e3018588d7840 says `Moved shared files into openam-shared`; these snapshots/imports/moves are rejected as BICs. For the primary's proposed BIC, `git show 4f04731207681973251c52436f07118e7c325e88 -- ...CsrfProtection.java ...OAuth2ConsentPageHelper.js ...main-authorize.js` proved that it newly wrote the secondary SSO-ID-as-CSRF mechanism, and `git ls-tree -r --name-only 3c076fc0dd1142d3c69fa39985667da2e1a8b628 --` for the two new files returned no paths, proving absence from that candidate's direct parent. `git cat-file commit 4f04731207681973251c52436f07118e7c325e88` confirmed parent 3c076fc0dd1142d3c69fa39985667da2e1a8b628, named human author/committer, and the trailer-free message `OPENAM-8575`; that marker evidence is valid only for the secondary mechanism, not the true headline BIC. `git show 2af597267e6eb9302f75445c2c726f9b84f62966` confirmed parent 97a34d9fee17395e8e052bfc45eb5855f436153e, replacement of the SSO-ID comparison with a 32-byte random token, removal of browser SSO-cookie retrieval for consent, SameSite=Lax, and protocol-derived Secure. The same diff deliberately retained com.sun.identity.cookie.httponly=false, and `git grep -n -F 'com.sun.identity.cookie.httponly=false' 16.1.1` found it at serverdefaults.properties:58. `git rev-parse '16.0.6^{commit}' '16.1.1^{commit}'` resolved 4529f108e9f5d3b8f98b4afb3dd035a3c4d73a1b and fe2271ec119e827b4252cec20293480322a84789. `git merge-base 4f04731207681973251c52436f07118e7c325e88 '16.0.6^{commit}'` returned the candidate, `git merge-base 2af597267e6eb9302f75445c2c726f9b84f62966 '16.0.6^{commit}'` returned the 16.0.6 commit rather than the fix, and the corresponding 16.1.1 check returned the direct fix, verifying the stated version boundary.
reasoning: The primary's NOT_AI result incorrectly promoted the reconstructable BIC of the advisory's secondary OAuth/OIDC coupling into the BIC of the whole vulnerability. Direct-parent absence and an AI-marker-free commit object make 4f04731207681973251c52436f07118e7c325e88 a sound NOT_AI finding for that secondary mechanism only; they do not resolve the earlier, independently exploitable HttpOnly=false initialization that the advisory names first, and that the claimed patched release still retains. The reviewer therefore wins the disputed verdict, introducer_sha, introducer_parent, parent-absence, and marker-state fields: the true headline BIC precedes the clone's parentless SVN snapshot boundary, so its SHA, immediate parent, parent-state check, and BIC-only AI evidence are unavailable. `introducer_parent_absent` is false rather than true because no eligible introducer and immediate parent were found; the proven absence in 3c076fc0dd1142d3c69fa39985667da2e1a8b628 pertains only to the rejected whole-case candidate. With no eligible headline BIC object, a closed NOT_AI judgment is not gate-complete, so the case is BLOCKED.
remaining_gap: The original pre-SVN-revision-389 commit that wrote com.sun.identity.cookie.httponly=false, its immediate parent, and its commit-object AI metadata are absent from the validated Git history. Closure requires older ForgeRock/OpenSSO SVN or CVS history that contains that actual change. Separately, although 16.1.1 contains direct fix 2af597267e6eb9302f75445c2c726f9b84f62966 for CSRF-token reuse, SameSite, and Secure defaults, its tree still ships HttpOnly=false, so the clone cannot substantiate complete removal of the advisory's headline condition at the claimed patch boundary.
